description: TIMCAT hosts a Nuclear Cost Estimation Tool for the capital cost of new nuclear power plants, published by the MIT Computational Reactor Physics Group with a citation to Stewart and Shirvan in Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews (2021). The README read on 2026-09-26 says the work was supported mainly by Fortum, with partial funding from US Department of Energy programmes, ARPA-E and EDF, and that users run cost_sensitivity.py after naming a basis table and input files. The inputs cover reference cost data for the PWR12-ME plant, with costs inflated from 1987 USD in the US Energy Economic Data Base to 2018 USD, a nine-tab workbook for direct costs, learning, modularisation and plant characteristics, scaling exponents, and labour, material and overrun indices. Access is a Python 3.9 package installed with pip from the GitHub source, with files in CSV and Excel format. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): MIT. Simulation uses are capacity planning and cost assessment of advanced reactors, for example sensitivity of overnight cost to learning and modular construction. Related records: model-cyclus-nuclear-fuel-cycle-simulator models fuel cycle scenarios and data-iaea-pris-power-reactor-information-system lists reactors in operation.
